title: The Email 3 Template: The Follow-Up That Books the Meetings
description: Belkins tracked 7.5 million cold emails: step 3 booked more meetings than steps 1 and 2 combined. Here's the email 3 template.
lead: This is the email 3 template from the reel. Most people stop after email 2, right before the email that books the most meetings.
insider: Every campaign we run has a planned follow-up sequence, with a new angle in each step. It's how one of our clients got **1,061 interested leads in a single quarter** at a 3.69% reply rate. Writing the sequence is half the job. Sending it on time to a clean list, every day, is the other half, and we handle both.

blocks.text: Belkins tracked 7.5 million cold emails in 2025. Email 1 had the best reply rate, but **step 3 alone booked more meetings than steps 1 and 2 combined**. People need a few touches before they say yes.

items: **A new angle.** Not "just bumping this to the top of your inbox".
**One proof.** A short result for a company like theirs.
**One tiny ask.** Easy to say yes to.

blocks.label: Email 3 template
blocks.text:
Subject: (keep the same thread)

Hi {first_name},

Different idea: [new angle: a problem or goal you didn't mention in emails 1 and 2].

We did this for [similar company type]: [one real result with a number].

Worth a 10-minute look?

[Your name]

blocks.label: Prompt
blocks.text:
Here are my cold email 1 and 2:
[paste them]

Write email 3 for the same prospect. Rules: under 70 words, a completely new angle, one real proof point I'll fill in, and a tiny yes/no question at the end. Never say "bumping this up" or "just following up". Give me 3 versions.
Space the emails 3 to 4 days apart. Stop the sequence the moment someone replies.

resources.name: Belkins
resources.note: Source of the 7.5 million email study (2025)

faq.q: How many emails should a sequence have?
faq.a: We usually run 3 to 4. After that, move people to a different channel like LinkedIn or try again in a few months.

faq.q: Should email 3 be a new subject line?
faq.a: Keep it in the same thread so they see the history. The new angle goes in the body.
